summary: Describes version 2 of the Internet Key Exchange protocol, used in IPsec for mutual authentication and for creating and maintaining security associations. It combines several earlier documents, including ISAKMP, IKE, the DOI, NAT traversal, legacy authentication, and remote address acquisition. IKEv2 does not interoperate with version 1 but can share the same UDP port. It was later replaced by RFC 5996.

plainLanguage.summary: IKEv2 is the IPsec protocol for authenticating peers and setting up security associations and keys. Its initial exchanges negotiate cryptographic settings, establish shared secret material, and create the first protected traffic association.

subtitle: IKEv2 negotiates keys and authentication for IPsec security associations.

tldr.problem: IPsec peers need shared keys and agreement about algorithms and traffic protections. Setting up this shared state manually does not scale well.
tldr.mechanism: IKEv2 exchanges requests and responses. IKE_SA_INIT negotiates algorithms and exchanges nonces and Diffie-Hellman values; IKE_AUTH authenticates the peers and establishes the first CHILD_SA for AH or ESP.
tldr.outcome: RFC 4306 obsoletes RFCs 2407, 2408, and 2409. It was itself obsoleted by RFC 5996 and updated by RFC 5282.

sections.title: The Initial IKE Exchanges
sections.content:
IKEv2 creates an IKE security association (IKE_SA) that holds shared secret information and cryptographic algorithms. The IKE_SA is used to establish security associations for ESP or AH; the RFC calls these CHILD_SAs.

The usual setup uses four messages in two request-response exchanges. IKE_SA_INIT negotiates algorithms, exchanges nonces, and performs a Diffie-Hellman exchange. IKE_AUTH exchanges identities and authentication proofs and establishes the first CHILD_SA. Parts of IKE_AUTH are encrypted and integrity-protected, which hides identities from eavesdroppers.
sections.plainLanguage: First, the peers agree on algorithms and create shared secret material. Then they authenticate each other and establish a security association for protected traffic.

sections.title: Later Exchanges and Message Reliability
sections.content:
After setup, either peer can use CREATE_CHILD_SA to establish or rekey a CHILD_SA. INFORMATIONAL exchanges can delete associations, report errors, or check whether a peer is still responding. Every IKE request expects a response.

IKE uses UDP and places responsibility for retransmission on the requester. If a response does not arrive before a timeout, the requester retransmits or abandons the connection. Each message includes a Message ID to match requests and responses and to recognize retransmissions. Implementations must handle IKE messages up to 1280 bytes and should handle messages up to 3000 bytes.
sections.plainLanguage: After the first setup, peers can create or replace traffic associations and exchange housekeeping messages. The requester retries when a response does not arrive.

sections.title: IKE Headers and Payloads
sections.content:
Each IKE message starts with a header containing the two peer SPIs, version, exchange type, flags, Message ID, and message length. The version in this RFC is major version 2 and minor version 0. The exchange type identifies whether the message belongs to IKE_SA_INIT, IKE_AUTH, CREATE_CHILD_SA, or INFORMATIONAL.

The header is followed by payloads that carry items such as security-association proposals, key-exchange values, identities, certificates, authentication data, traffic selectors, and notifications. A payload's Next Payload field identifies what follows it. After the initial exchanges, messages are protected using negotiated encryption and integrity keys.
sections.plainLanguage: The header identifies the IKE association and the exchange being performed. Payloads carry the negotiation, identity, authentication, or traffic-selection data for that step.

sections.title: Key Derivation and Authentication
sections.content:
IKE derives keying material from the nonces and Diffie-Hellman shared secret using the negotiated pseudorandom function. It creates separate keys for encryption and integrity in each direction, as well as a key used to derive keys for CHILD_SAs.

Peers authenticate with signatures, a shared secret, or an Extensible Authentication Protocol method. The RFC warns that a shared secret derived from a password or other low-entropy value is not secure against dictionary attacks. It also requires strong random values and says implementations must not use certain null algorithms for the IKE_SA.
sections.plainLanguage: The peers derive different keys for protecting messages in each direction and for creating traffic associations. Authentication proves identity, and weak passwords or poor randomness can undermine the result.

sections.title: NAT Traversal and Conformance
sections.content:
IKEv2 can negotiate UDP encapsulation of IKE and ESP packets to help them pass through Network Address Translators (NATs). NAT detection notifications are exchanged during IKE_SA_INIT. If a NAT is detected, the peers send later IKE and ESP traffic for that IKE_SA over UDP port 4500. NAT traversal support is optional.

A minimal implementation can omit several optional features, including NAT traversal and requesting a temporary internal address. All implementations must be able to complete the basic four-message exchange and respond to INFORMATIONAL exchanges. The RFC notes that IKEv2 does not interoperate with IKE version 1, although both can use the same UDP port.
sections.plainLanguage: When a NAT is on the path, IKEv2 can carry IKE and ESP packets over UDP port 4500. This support is optional, and IKEv2 does not interoperate with IKE version 1.

viz.caption: The four messages in the typical IKEv2 setup

messages.label: IKE_SA_INIT request
messages.note: Offers algorithms and sends a Diffie-Hellman value and nonce.

messages.label: IKE_SA_INIT response
messages.note: Selects algorithms and sends its Diffie-Hellman value and nonce.

messages.label: IKE_AUTH request
messages.note: Sends identity, authentication, and the first CHILD_SA proposal.

messages.label: IKE_AUTH response
messages.note: Sends identity, authentication, and the accepted CHILD_SA.
